impact.rationale: The patch defines source, formatter, official package-selection, exact Go-event, compatibility, and artifact-publication gates for a privileged revocation-sensitive subscription refresh backend. A false acceptance or privacy leak would undermine the evidence used for integration.

regressionLikelihood.rationale: No remaining source-visible defect was found after the v1 ordering and v2 raw-artifact corrections. Risk remains because the 25-path gate patch and paired 24-path Go overlay have not executed together on the exact Linux head.

regressionProtection.rationale: All 271 declared pure-CPU models pass independently, exact source membership and upload allowlists are closed, and v1/v2 regression cases are explicit. The dedicated v3 lane is ordinary-only: exact-head Linux formatting, official selection, seven-package compilation/ordinary tests, and fresh readback have not run; race and typed failure diagnosis are separate open work.

recoverability.rationale: The non-Go patch has no migration or persistent runtime state and can be reverted before promotion. It only enables evidence workflows and readers; production/runtime defaults remain unchanged.

confidence.rationale: The exact full and v2-to-v3 patch bytes, base, convergent candidate tree, 25 paths, manifest afterimages, three upload allowlists, runner-local raw streams, control-flow ordering, source counts, pins, and all 271 CPU models were inspected. Runtime acceptance is explicitly unresolved.

applicability.rationale: The patch adds the dedicated P207A lane and updates every identified normal/profile/apply/service/UNKNOWN/Completion source contract affected by the 24-path Go overlay.

statusQuoRisk.rationale: The risk of retaining b5 without P207A depends on backend revocation and durability semantics, outside this non-Go component review.

materialBoundaries.invariant: Formatting and Go evidence must be captured before independent strict acceptance gates.
materialBoundaries.counterexample: An early non-empty gofmt assertion would prevent Go execution and event capture.
materialBoundaries.legitimateControl: The workflow captures format and Go exit under set +e, records source-after and event-reader status, then applies format, Go, event, and stderr gates; early-gate and reorder mutations are rejected.

materialBoundaries.invariant: Raw Go event and stderr streams stay runner-local and uploads use closed explicit path sets.
materialBoundaries.counterexample: Adding raw go-events.private.jsonl, go.stderr, or a directory glob could publish arbitrary failed-test output.
materialBoundaries.legitimateControl: All three artifact names map to exact allowlists; raw basenames and glob markers are rejected, while execution and reader markers prove raw streams remain local inputs. Three concrete negatives hit the intended ContractError gates.

materialBoundaries.invariant: The lane binds exact module, fixture, changed-Go, formatter, package, test-file, top-name, and run-name sets.
materialBoundaries.counterexample: Count-only substitutions could omit an affected path or top.
materialBoundaries.legitimateControl: The checker recomputes content hashes and exact ordered sets for module825, fixture20, changed24, seven packages, source486, run481, and foundation689/previous688.

materialBoundaries.invariant: Linux/amd64 Go 1.23.12 must select and complete all seven packages and 481 required tops with zero skip/fail and fresh-source identity.
materialBoundaries.counterexample: Build tags or compilation can invalidate static membership, and a run can omit or fail a required top.
materialBoundaries.legitimateControl: Pinned official go list and JSON event readers enforce exact selection and terminals, but the exact head has not yet produced those artifacts.

materialBoundaries.invariant: A failing ordinary run must stay failed without publishing raw output; this source slice does not claim typed failure-cause localization.
materialBoundaries.runtimeRoot: .github/workflows/chengwang-subscription-refresh.yml final gates and bounded failure artifact
materialBoundaries.counterexample: Exit-only evidence can prove rejection but cannot distinguish compile, test assertion, timeout, or other Go failure cause.
materialBoundaries.legitimateControl: The captured Go and event-reader exit codes cannot become pass, source/format custody remains bounded, and raw streams are not uploaded. Typed privacy-safe diagnosis is explicitly deferred rather than inferred.

materialBoundaries.invariant: New sources and top 689 propagate without deleting prior 688 or rewriting historical OLD_V5 anchors.
materialBoundaries.counterexample: A dedicated-only update could leave a stale downstream reader.
materialBoundaries.legitimateControl: All changed Go paths are represented in imported source closures; full FMT producer/reader agree at 50, prior688 remains pinned, and OLD_V5 plus active five-file anchors are unchanged.

materialBoundaries.invariant: Source closure must not enable production refresh by default.
materialBoundaries.counterexample: A gate patch could also alter runtime activation.
materialBoundaries.legitimateControl: The exact paths are workflows, readers, contracts, and models; no product Go default or production environment is changed.
